title: Commit-log sidecar + span-forwarder to guarantee deterministic telemetry commits for inference requests
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Our inference stack currently emits OTLP spans and Prometheus-style metrics from multiple components (gateway, runtime, batchers). In high-throughput and multi-tenant scenarios we observe partial or out-of-order metric commits when transient failures, retries, or batching reorder events. This causes unstable per-request KPIs (per-token latency, cost attribution) and makes SLOs noisy for customers.

Goal: Implement a lightweight commit-log sidecar (telemetry commit-log) co-located with inference node processes that provides: deterministic, idempotent commits for metric and span fragments; deterministic ordering for per-request KPI reconstruction; resilient forwarder with backpressure and exponential backoff; a span-forwarder mode that guarantees sampling decision propagation to downstream consumers. The sidecar should integrate with OTLP Prometheus exporters and expose a compatibility shim for existing collectors so we can roll it out incrementally.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Sidecar accepts OTLP metrics and traces on 0.0.0.0:4317 and a Prometheus scrape-compatible /metrics-forward endpoint.
2) Each telemetry fragment is appended to a local append-only commit-log (file-backed or Kafka-compatible) with idempotency key derived from request_id + sequence.
3) Downstream exporter emits in-ordered, deduplicated telemetry to central ingest.
4) Canary rollout on 5% of inference nodes for 48h shows <1% increase in p99 latency and reduces out-of-order/incomplete per-request KPI events by >90%.
5) Backpressure path: when central ingest is unavailable the sidecar persists up to N MB (configurable) and exposes a health signal used by orchestrator to route new requests away from the node.
6) Tests: unit+integration for idempotency, ordering, retry, and sampling-decision propagation.
7) Documentation: operator runbook, config reference, and dashboard tiles for visibility.
design_notes:
Architecture: The sidecar will run as a Unix process alongside the inference runtime. In broad strokes: 
- Accept OTLP gRPC/HTTP (4317) and a Prom scrape-forward endpoint for legacy flows.
- Normalize incoming telemetry into a canonical envelope (tenant_id, request_id, fragment_index, total_fragments, timestamp, payload_type).
- Append envelopes to a local commit-log implemented initially as a write-ahead-file with rotation and background compaction. The WAL format will include checksums and an idempotency index (embedded small hash map persisted to disk).
- A forwarder worker streams committed envelopes to central ingest (OTLP collector or Kafka topic) in strictly increasing fragment_index order per request_id. Forwarder ensures exactly-once semantics via idempotency keys.
- If central ingest rejects or connectivity fails, sidecar will exponentially backoff and keep local queue up to storage_quota. Beyond quota it sets a diagnostic health flag and increments node-level "telemetry.commit_log.backpressure" metric to signal orchestrator.
- Span sampling decisions will be carried as metadata fields; when downstream consumers request sampled spans the sidecar will attach the sampling decision and ensure sampled fragments are retained until accepted.

Implementation choices: start with file-backed WAL to reduce dependencies, providing a pluggable delivery backend interface so we can switch to Kafka/NSQ if we need cross-host guarantees. Use protobuf for envelope schema. The idempotency index will be sharded by tenant to bound memory.

Schema: proto v1 telemetry.CommitEnvelope { string tenant_id = 1; string request_id = 2; uint32 fragment_index = 3; uint32 total_fragments = 4; int64 timestamp_ms = 5; bytes otlp_payload = 6; map<string,string> meta = 7; }
implementation_tasks:
- wire OTLP receiver into sidecar binary and basic pass-through (Samuel)
- implement WAL writer with rotation and checksum (TBD)
- idempotency index and per-tenant sharding (Riya)
- forwarder worker with backpressure and retry policy (Samuel)
- prometheus scrape compatibility endpoint and metrics for internal health (Jamal)
- operator flags + config (max_storage_mb, retry_policy, snapshot_interval) (Ops)
- integration tests: local ingest mock, WAL corruption scenarios, backpressure threshold test (CI)
- docs: runbook + config reference + phasing plan (Aisha)
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 - dev: sidecar runs in dev clusters with file-backed WAL, no traffic routing changes. Validate correctness with synthetic traffic.
Phase 1 - internal canary: deploy to 5% of nodes (non-customer) for 1 week. Observe ordering/dedup and p99 impact.
Phase 2 - customer canary: select low-risk customers serve through nodes with sidecar. Monitor per-request KPI completeness and error budgets.
Phase 3 - gradual ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with telemetry gating. Rollback: disable forwarder and let WAL drain to central ingest; if storage_quota often reached, revert routing.
Monitoring gates: p99 latency delta < 3ms, telemetry.incomplete_fragments_rate < 1% after forwarder enabled, commit_log.backpressure_count < 0.5/min.
test_plan:
Unit tests for WAL append/rotate/repair. Fuzz tests for partial write and truncate. Integration test: local mock-ingest that randomly NACKs certain fragments to exercise retry and ordering. End-to-end test: synthetic multi-fragment requests through runtime->sidecar->central-ingest verifying reconstructed per-request KPIs match expected values. Load test: sustain 5k req/s on a single node with configured fragment distribution.
Failure tests: simulate central ingest outage and ensure sidecar toggles health flag and orchestrator routes away; simulate WAL corruption and ensure repair path recovers and refuses startup on unrecoverable corruption.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Critical metrics to emit from sidecar:
- telemetry.commit_log.append_rate (counter)
- telemetry.commit_log.forward_rate (counter)
- telemetry.commit_log.dedupe_count (counter)
- telemetry.commit_log.backpressure_count (gauge)
- telemetry.commit_log.disk_usage_bytes (gauge)
- telemetry.commit_log.unacked_fragments (gauge)
- telemetry.commit_log.forward_error_rate (counter)

Suggested alerts:
- commit_log.disk_usage_bytes > 80% quota for 5m -> Pager
- forward_error_rate spike > 1/min for 5m -> P1
- backpressure_count > 0 for > 2m -> P1
- unacked_fragments growth rate > 10% over 1h -> investigate ingestion bottleneck
